授業計画
1. General introduction Interdisciplinary study
Eljamal Osama, Spring Mark Andrew
Provide lectures and discussions on "Analytics and Ranking Systems".
2. ’General introduction interdisciplinary study’ and ’Lesson for active learning and researching (I)’
Michitaka Ohtaki, Akira Harata
･ Former half: Introduction of Interdisciplinary Graduate School of Engineering Sciences;
Historical background and current landscape of IGSES is presented in terms of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary studies in science and engineering.
･ Latter half: Lesson for active learning and researching (I)
“Today's targets”, “near future target: exercise of lesson 2-2”, and “future target in 2028 spring” are presented and a training chance is given to use the databases such as Scopus, Web of Science, SciFinder-n, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, researchmap, KAKEN and so on, when time allows. The exercise of lesson 2-2 is a report of the following two topics: (1) Research trends after your birth on keywords of possible Master thesis topics of your own: survey results by yourself. (2) (a) Information (title, authors, journal name, published year, etc.) of the most notable paper for you, among the papers on the topics published in these two years. (b) Short summary of the abstract and short comments on the points you focus on it.
Essentials: Bring a note- or tablet-PC connectable to wireless LAN (kitenet, edunet, eduroam, wi-fi, etc.). Bringing only a smartphone is not recommended.
To be continued to lesson 8.
3. Elements of international collaboration among industry, academia and government
Yuichi Harada
Students learn the followings: the significance and attitude to participate in industry-academia-government joint research; examples of doctoral student enrollment, career support joint research program and internship experiences utilizing the seeds-search program of next-generation basic technologies; and guidance for learning how to handle intellectual properties. The education curriculum at the Robert Fan / Entrepreneurship Center, which supports students’ independent research and entrepreneurship activities, will also be explained. Regarding international cooperation, the Campus Asia Education Program and the Green Asia Education Program will be outlined. Students will be encouraged to participate in these programs. Furthermore, the two international conferences, “Cross-Straits Symposium on Energy and Environmental Science and Technology (CSS-EEST)” and “International Exchange and Innovation Conference on Engineering & Sciences (IEICES)”, held annually by the graduate school, will be outlined. Students will be encouraged to presents their research achievements at the symposium and conference.
Essentials: Bring a note- or tablet-PC connectable to wireless LAN (kitenet, edunet, eduroam, wi-fi, etc.). Bringing only a smartphone is not recommended.
4. Elements of ICT for D
Kai Morino, Reo Kai
Students learn the followings: fundamentals of ICT for D and its future developments; how to learn ICT for D; basic knowledge for improving skills of ICT for D.
5, 6, 7. Elements of interdisciplinary developments
Kohei Kusada, Kazunari Katayama, Naoki Ikegaya
Students learn the outline and related cutting-edge topics for each of the three categories corresponding to “materials”, “energy” and “environment” in our graduate school.
8. Lesson for active learning and researching (II)
Akira Harata
Presentation of your reports for lesson 2-2
Everyone whose student-ID has four digits listed separately is expected to make a short presentation about hers/his report in order (Please excuse if time is up). Reports will be shared on screen with the caution: “No photos or video allowed”.
